_what: the rung-4 safety factor and the D196 (1) Gate A would-have-missed count, re-derived from the PER-REQUEST observed-over-predicted first-token ratio of the committed healthy-window robot rows of the rung-3 sent cells, seeds 4 to 7
_only_the_input_changed: q90 unchanged, nearest-rank rule unchanged (the committed d190_measured_safety._nearest_rank is CALLED, not copied), overrun formula unchanged, MARGIN_CF unchanged

old_input_for_comparison.verdict: IDENTITY: q90 of 5 points by nearest rank IS the maximum, so overrun = (max - q90) * predicted is identically 0 and the committed would-have-missed 0 of 6 could not have been anything else

THE_GATE._status: D206: THE GATE. Exposure and overrun magnitude, both measurements.
THE_GATE._how_to_read: a deferral placed at the latest safe start carries about the exposure probability of overrunning, and the overrun costs (ratio - safety_factor) x predicted service seconds; both are measured on real sent requests, which the retired count was not

_why_the_count_is_retired: D206, on this script's own reasoning: overrun = (b - SAFETY_FACTOR) * service has the sign of (b - SAFETY_FACTOR) alone, so the count is 0 or N and never in between. The old 0 of 6 was an identity because q90 equalled max; N of N at the max bias is an identity of the opposite sign. Replacing the input made the QUANTILE real and did not make the COUNT informative. The column is kept and labelled so a reader can see why it was retired, not merely that it went.

gate_a_count_is_structurally_0_or_N.why: overrun = (b - SAFETY_FACTOR) * predicted_total_service_s with a positive service, so the sign is the sign of (b - SAFETY_FACTOR) and is the same for every deferral. The count is 0 below the factor, 0 AT the factor and N above it, for any N.
gate_a_count_is_structurally_0_or_N.consequence: the old 0 of 6 was an identity because q90 EQUALLED max; the new N of N at the max bias is an identity of the opposite sign. Replacing the input makes the QUANTILE real and does NOT make the COUNT informative. Read `exposure_measured_on_sent_requests` instead.
gate_a_count_is_structurally_0_or_N.register: the 6 is the committed and independently reproduced rd_question_defers counter; only 1 of the 6 carries predicted_total_service_s in the committed proof JSON, so the per-deferral overrun seconds are reported for that one and the COUNTS are reported by the sign rule above, which is exact for all 6

exposure_measured_on_sent_requests._what: the quantity the would-have-missed COUNT cannot carry: how often a sent recall request really did overrun the safety factor, measured on the committed cells
exposure_measured_on_sent_requests._how_to_read_it: a deferral placed at the latest safe start carries about this probability of overrunning, and the overrun magnitude is (ratio - safety_factor) x predicted service seconds
exposure_measured_on_sent_requests._why_the_count_is_not_this: the count compares ONE bias against the factor, so it is 0 or N by the sign of (b - factor); this fraction compares EVERY measured request against the factor

_register.at_q90_column: AN IDENTITY BY DESIGN and labelled as one: the bias equals the safety factor, so the overrun is identically 0. It is reported so the reader can see which column is an identity.
_register.at_median_and_at_max_columns: MEASUREMENTS, because the median and the max are strictly different from the q90 on an n of 463 with 46 rows strictly above the q90
_register.rows_are_per_request_not_per_cell: the old 5 values were the sent rows of TWO devices on TWO seeds; these are every sent robot request on FOUR seeds
